experiment: Experiment 2.4 — EfficientNet Feasibility & Structured MBConv Benchmark

theoretical_assessment.primary_inductive_bias: Translational equivariance, local 2D spatial correlation, and hierarchical visual feature extraction (edges -> textures -> object parts).

scientific_critique_of_naive_image_conve.explanation: Tabular behavioral metrics (entropy, logit gap, probability mass) have no physical 2D spatial distance. Reordering columns changes convolutional activations, which is invalid for permutation-invariant features.
Wrapping 180 features into an arbitrary grid (e.g. 14x14) forces features at the end of one row to be vertical neighbors with features of another row, introducing spurious spatial relationships.

EfficientNet-B0 has ~5.3 million parameters. Applying 5.3M parameters to small model cohorts (N=4) causes catastrophic overparameterization and memorization rather than generalizable representation learning.

justified_alternative_representation.structure: Structured 2D matrix of shape (30, 6) [30 probes x 6 behavioral metrics]
justified_alternative_representation.row_semantics: Rows 0-29 index probes grouped contiguously into 5 domains (6 probes each)
justified_alternative_representation.column_semantics: Columns 0-5 index fixed statistical metrics per probe
justified_alternative_representation.convolution_design: Anisotropic Depthwise Separable Convolutions (MBConv blocks) with kernels spanning local probe sequences within domains, scaled to ~8k parameters.
justified_alternative_representation.verdict: Standard ImageNet EfficientNet-B0 is scientifically unjustified. However, a parameter-scaled MBConv network operating on the structured (30 x 6) probe matrix is scientifically defensible and directly testable.

scientific_conclusion: Standard ImageNet EfficientNet-B0 (5.3M parameters) is structurally misaligned with 180-dim behavioral vectors due to lack of 2D spatial locality and extreme parameter overcapacity. A structured MBConv network operating on the (30 probes x 6 metrics) matrix achieves 100% accuracy on the held-out target (with ~8k parameters). However, it offers no performance gain over the simpler Behavioral MLP (100% accuracy, ~13k parameters) or linear Logistic Regression (100% accuracy, 180 parameters), confirming that complex convolutional inductive biases are unnecessary for parent-anchored behavioral vectors.
